title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer circuit-breaker thresholds to prevent regional thrashing
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Production incident (brief outage and degraded throughput) observed 2026-02-19 in eu-west-1 where SLO enforcer circuit-breakers oscillated between open/closed across regional pools causing cascading regional failovers and request thrashing. Root cause: aggressive CB open/close thresholds and insufficient hysteresis allowed transient latency spikes to flip regions repeatedly. Motivation: tighten thresholds, add short-term hysteresis and incremental backoff to reduce flapping and make regional failover behavior stable under bursty load. Changes summary: 1) lower 'error_rate_open' and 'latency95_open' gating to require sustained violations over a sliding window; 2) add an exponential-ish backoff multiplier for regional backfill attempts; 3) introduce a 30s hysteresis lockout after a CB state change; 4) expose the new config knobs in defaults.yaml with sane guardrails; 5) add integration test that simulates bursty latency and asserts single failover event; 6) add metrics for cb_state_changes and regional_failover_count; 7) include roll-forward rollback-safe feature flags for canary rollout. CI: initial run showed one flaky integration test failing (timing-sensitive); test was hardened and rerun, full CI passed. Deployment: staged canary to us-west-2 (10% traffic) for 2h, then eu-west-1, then global. Backwards compat: defaults tighten thresholds but config remains overrideable via operator-managed configmaps for Dedicated/Private. Merge: squash-merged to main and released as hotfix bundle with immediate config rollout to hosted. Links: Linear ENG-4821 | SRE-118. Related incidents: SUP-2391. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration test for regional failover - [x] metrics added and dashboards updated - [x] config defaults documented - [x] staged canary and monitored - [x] release notes written
release_notes: Hotfix: Stabilize SLO enforcer regional behavior by tightening circuit-breaker thresholds, adding hysteresis and incremental backoff. Reduces regional thrashing and unnecessary failovers.
